[EVALUATION RESULT]
Question: Consider the standard Bruin–Troubetzkoy family of interval translation mappings (ITMs). Restrict to the set of parameter values for which the associated ITM is of infinite type; here, “almost every” on this set refers to the natural probability measure supported on this zero-Lebesgue-measure subset. Which strongest conclusion holds for almost every such parameter value?
Predicted label: 'E'
Predicted text: 'For almost every parameter in the Bruin–Troubetzkoy family that defines an ITM of infinite type (with respect to the natural probability measure on the infinite-type locus), the resulting interval translation mapping is ergodic.'
Correct label: 'B'
Correct text: 'For almost every parameter in the Bruin–Troubetzkoy family that defines an ITM of infinite type (with respect to the natural probability measure on the infinite-type locus), the resulting interval translation mapping is weakly mixing.'
Exact Match: 0.0
